newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 15.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Friday:
* The European tradition of the long summer shutdown is ending as European companies struggle to remain competitive.
* W.R. Grace agreed to sell its packaging business.
* New York State's Comptroller sued 11 Columbia/HCA former executives and directors of the company.
* The FCC approved Bell Atlantic's merger with NYNEX.
* Consumer prices climbed 0.2 percent in July, while industrial production rose 0.2 percent.
* PepsiCo said it expects $4.5 billion in cash from the spinoff of its restaurant business.
* Travelers Group named Thomas Jones head of its fee-based asset-management business.
* Indonesia floated the rupiah, which fell sharply against the dollar.
* United Parcel Service and its Teamsters union resumed their talks.
* Kodak plans to place its name on 300 to 500 speciality stores across the U.S. in the next 18 months.
* Hugo Boss made uniforms for the Nazis, s spokeswoman acknowledged.
* A big U.S. auto dealer pleaded guilty to mail fraud in a case in which he was accused of bribing Honda executives.
